facts.text: The vehicle network is the wiring and message system through which a machine's computers communicate; J1939 is the standard dialect heavy machines use on that network, including requests to slow or stop.
facts.quote: The vehicle network is the wiring and message system through which a machine's computers talk to one another, and J1939 is the standard dialect heavy machines use on it, including for the message that asks the machine to slow or stop.

facts.text: SAE J1939, from SAE International, defines heavy-duty vehicle message formats so that a brake controller from one supplier can understand a speed message from another.
facts.quote: SAE J1939, from SAE International, defines how heavy-duty vehicles format those messages so that a brake controller from one supplier understands a speed message from another.

facts.text: A DBC file specifies which bus messages carry which signals, the meanings of their bits, and scaling into physical units; without the correct DBC file, a recorded bus log is unreadable numbers.
facts.quote: A DBC file is the dictionary for a bus: which message carries which signal, which bits mean what, and how to scale them into physical units. Without the right DBC file a recorded bus log is unreadable numbers.

facts.text: The technical specification ISO/TS 21815-2:2021 defines the on-board J1939 interface between a collision-avoidance device and the machine, including slow-down, controlled-stop and emergency-stop commands, capability discovery and a keep-alive signal.
facts.quote: ISO/TS 21815-2:2021 defines the on-board J1939 interface between a collision-avoidance device and the machine, with commands to slow down, perform a controlled stop or an emergency stop, plus capability discovery and a keep-alive signal

facts.text: The collision-avoidance device-to-machine J1939 interface defined by ISO/TS 21815-2:2021 is not plug-and-play.
The bus carrying brake requests is a safety and security interface: spoofed or stale messages, bus faults and incompatible implementations must not create unsafe brake commands.
facts.quote: Because the brake request travels on this bus, it is a safety and security interface: spoofed or stale messages, bus faults and incompatible implementations must not create unsafe brake commands [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The minimum machine-state recording list from CAN or J1939 includes speed, gear, steering or articulation angle, yaw rate, brake command and measured brake pressure, payload and attachment positions; DBC and message-schema versions must be recorded alongside.
facts.quote: Machine state from CAN or J1939 is on the minimum recording list: speed, gear, steering or articulation angle, yaw rate, brake command and measured brake pressure, payload and attachment positions, with DBC and message-schema versions recorded alongside [Chapter 7].

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop benches emulate the rest of the machine's network traffic and the brake-request interface.
facts.quote: Hardware-in-the-loop benches emulate the rest of the network traffic and the brake-request interface [Chapters 7, 11].

facts.text: If the collision system acts through the J1939 interface, validation must include end-to-end integration latency.
facts.quote: If the system acts through the J1939 interface, validation must include end-to-end integration latency

facts.text: Recorded bus data allow engineers to reconstruct time to collision, zone entry and braking after the event.
facts.quote: the recorded bus data are what let engineers reconstruct time to collision, zone entry and braking afterwards [Chapters 7, 10].
